blocks.text: With David's mortality becoming apparent—he can no longer maintain body heat even when covered—multiple factions mobilize to secure their favored successor. Adonijah publicly moves first, organizing chariots, horsemen, and a display of force, then staging a feast that includes his older brother's supporters and the officials of Judah. However, key figures remain outside this coalition: the priest Zadok, Benaiah the commander, the prophet Nathan, and Solomon himself are pointedly excluded from Adonijah's celebration. Nathan responds by prompting Bathsheba to approach the aging David, reminding him of an oath regarding Solomon's succession. This chapter sets in motion the contested succession that drives the opening movement of First Kings.
